source.title: Seesaw: Accelerating Training by Balancing Learning Rate and Batch Size Scheduling
source.authors: Alexandru Meterez; Depen Morwani; Jing-Feng Wu; Costin-Andrei Oncescu; Cengiz Pehlevan; S. Kakade

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Compares batch-size schedules and reports validation loss, a different setup from the version's cited fixed-epoch comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation losses for batch sizes and schedules. It does not report training error or a train–test gap; its results bear on V5's held-out-performance component. Figure-only curves are not transcribed into numerical rows.
record.test_reason: Tests V5 in C4 language-model pretraining: fixed-batch runs process the same token budget within each model size, and batch-ramp runs are compared at equal FLOPs and token exposure. Validation loss measures V5's held-out-performance outcome; a training–test gap is not required.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: Seesaw approximately preserves cosine-schedule performance while reducing serial training steps by about 36%. Qualify this by the demonstrated batch-size regime; sufficiently large starting batches and overly aggressive ramps underperform. The reported serial-step reduction does not independently establish a measured hardware wall-clock speedup.
record.recipe_differences: Tests batch-size scheduling and validation loss under language-model pretraining, rather than the cited fixed-epoch large-batch generalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size relative to critical batch size, schedule choice, model size, and weight decay; the paper reports worse performance past critical batch size and that increasingly aggressive schedules can underperform.

fits_no_version.finding: Theoretical equivalence bounds for SGD and normalized SGD on noisy linear regression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under specified bounded-risk and variance-dominance assumptions, learning-rate decay and batch ramps can yield population risks within constant factors at matched sample exposure.

record.problems: No training-error values or train–test gaps are reported. Validation-loss differences have no uncertainty estimates. Much of the batch-size evidence concerns comparisons to the 128 batch setting and does not isolate a fixed-epoch generalization effect.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 2 schedule variants and Figure 3 beyond-critical-batch curves were not entered because their individual curve values are figure-only in the supplied text; Figure 3 is described textually as showing growing discrepancy with larger batch sizes.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under different tuning budgets.

Image classifiers; longer-training mitigation; normalization changes; independent causal effects of warmup or learning-rate scaling. The study tests matched token exposure rather than reporting epoch counts.
Dropout effects and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Qualitative validation-loss comparison showing naive fixed-learning-rate batch doubling substantially underperforms learning-rate decay and Seesaw, for initial batches 128 and 256. This result is not covered by rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: All table values match the supplied text. Seesaw batch labels denote initial batches, whereas cosine batches remain fixed. Matched token budgets provide the exposure control relevant to V5; missing training losses do not invalidate that test. Near-matching a cosine run at the same initial batch does not show recovery of the best smaller-batch loss. Figures 2 and 3 are already declared in rows_left_out and therefore are not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and generalization on natural labels.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Comparisons of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
Training–test gap; language models; fixed-epoch comparison to smaller batches; the cited mitigation methods beyond Seesaw scheduling.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
